result.topic_en: A table giving, for each small positive or negative integer D, the linear forms (residue classes) that contain every number modulo which D is a quadratic residue, to be used to exclude candidate factors when factoring numbers.

methods.what: Characterisation of the moduli for which a given integer D is a quadratic residue: all such numbers lie in specified residue classes modulo 4|D| (or |D|), used to exclude trial divisors when factoring
methods.quote:
Formae quibus continentur {+omnes+} numeri, quorum multi-
plici, si superaddas aut inde subducas numerum da-
tum, vel ipsum, vel {+in+} qu[-o-]{+em+}cunque quadratum ductum
numerus quadratus potest effici.

methods.what: -1 is a quadratic residue only for numbers of the form 4k+1
2 is a quadratic residue only for numbers of the form 8k±1
-2 is a quadratic residue only for numbers of the form 8k+1, 8k+3
-3 is a quadratic residue only for numbers of the form 3k+1
3 is a quadratic residue only for numbers of the form 12k±1
Table of residue classes for primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 (D = +p, classes ±r mod p) and p ≡ 3 mod 4 (D = −p, classes +r mod p)
Table of residue classes modulo 4|D| for composite or even D (e.g. ±5, ±6, ±10, ±14, ±22, ±26)
